<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par48 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=19}}; in Niphʿal {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּֽׁבְעָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=23}}. Cf., however, also {{GHGheb|text=מִכְרָה|translate=sell}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=25|verse=31}}, notwithstanding the impf. {{GHGheb|text=יִמְכֹּר}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֶרְכָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=5}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=עִרְכוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=3}}), but impf. {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲרֹךְ}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽסְפָה|translate=collect}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=16}} (for {{GHGheb|text=אִס׳}} cf. {{GHGpar|63|l}} and the plural {{GHGheb|text=אִסְפוּ}}), but 2nd masc. {{GHGheb|text=אֱסֹף}}; {{GHGheb|text=נִצְּרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=141|verse=3}}. Barth (see above, {{GHGpar|47|i}} note) finds in these forms a trace of old imperfects in ''i'', cf. {{GHGpar|63|n}}. On the other hand, {{GHGheb|text=קָרְבָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=69|verse=19}} (also Imperat. {{GHGheb|text=קְרַב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=9|verse=7}}, &c.), but impf. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרַב}}. Without {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, we have the form {{GHGheb|text=לְךָ|translate=go}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=25|verse=17}}. The form {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}} in pause becomes {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹ֫לָה}}, the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}} becomes {{GHGheb|text=קְטָ֫לָה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יְרָ֫שָׁה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=23}}. But also without the pause we find {{GHGheb|text=מְ֫לוֹכָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=8}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} and {{GHGheb|text=צְרוֹפָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=26|verse=2}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, on which see {{GHGpar|46|e}}. On the other hand {{GHGheb|text=רְגָ֫זָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=פְּשֹׁ֫טָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֹ֫רָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֲג֫וֹרָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=32|verse=11}} are to be explained as aramaizing forms of the 2nd plur. fem.; also for {{GHGheb|text=חִרְדוּ}} v. 11 read {{GHGheb|text=חֲרָ֫דָה}}, and for {{GHGheb|text=סֹֽפְדִים}} v. 12 read {{GHGheb|text=סְפֹ֫דָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|k}}
The shortened imperative is found only in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, e.g. in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=גַּל}} from {{GHGheb|text=גַּלֵּה}}. The shade of meaning conveyed by the imperatives with {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} is not always so perceptible as in the cohortative forms of the imperfect, but the longer form is frequently emphatic, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קוּם|translate=rise up}}, {{GHGheb|text=ק֫וּמָה|translate=up!}} {{GHGheb|text=תֵּן|translate=give}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּנָה|translate=give up!}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|l}}
Rem. The form {{GHGheb|text=דְּעֶה}} for {{GHGheb|text=דְּעָה}}, best attested in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=14}} (where it is taken by the Masora as imperat., not as infin., {{GHGheb|text=דַּעָה}}) is evidently due to the influence of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} which follows it in close connexion (so Strack, on the analogy of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=2}}); for other examples of this change of ''a'' to S<sup>e</sup>ghol, see above, under d, {{GHGpar|73|d}}, and {{GHGpar|80|i}}. On the other hand, it is doubtful whether {{GHGheb|text=רַבֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=29}} (from {{GHGheb|text=רָבָה}}) is intended for {{GHGheb|text=רַבָּה}}, and not rather for the common form of the imperative {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=רַבֵּה}}. In favour of the former explanation it may be urged that the imperative {{GHGheb|text=צֵ֫אָה}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָצָא}}) follows immediately after; in favour of the latter, that the ending {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, with imperatives of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, is not found elsewhere, and also that here no guttural follows (as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=14}}).<section end=par48 />

<section begin=par49 />{{GHGpar-heading|49|The Perfect and Imperfect with Wāw Consecutive}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|a}}
'''1.''' The use of the two tense-forms, as is shown more fully in the Syntax (§§ 106, 107, cf. above, § 47, note on ''a''), is by no means restricted to the expression of the past or future. One of the most striking peculiarities in the Hebrew ''consecution'' of tenses<ref>The other Semitic languages do not exhibit this peculiarity, excepting the Phoenician, the most closely related to Hebrew, and of course the Moabitish dialect of the ''Mêšaʿ'' inscription, which is practically identical with Old Hebrew. Lpz. 18S6 ff.}}}} 1908, p. 379) where we find {{GHGheb|text=ואשׂא ידי}} ''and I lifted up my hand'', {{GHGheb|text=ויענני|translate=and he answered me}}, after a perfect of narration.</ref> is the phenomenon that, in representing a series of past events, only the first<section end=par49 /><noinclude>
